# Volume 3 — Chapter XL A Book of Revelation

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

For the summer, the Irvings returned to Echo Cottage, where Nell enjoyed a delightful three-week stay during July. No change had come over Miss Rosalind; although Belinda the Fourth had become a quite mature young woman by this time, her affectionate devotion to Nell remained genuine.
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0000 }

“Taking everything into account, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, I haven’t come across a single person in Boston who compares to you,” she declared openly.
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0001 }

Cedric had nearly reached adulthood as well. Having reached the age of sixteen, he now sported short-cut brown hair instead of his former chestnut curls, and his enthusiasm for football had surpassed his interest in fairies. Even so, the connection that linked him to his former instructor remained intact. It is only kindred spirits that remain unaltered as time passes.
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0002 }

It was a dreary, harsh, and rain-soaked July evening when Nell returned to Grey Shutters. The ocean was being battered by one of those violent summer storms that occasionally rush across the gulf. The initial drops of rain struck the windows just as Nell entered.
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0003 }

“Did Cedric bring you back?” Thirza inquired. “You should have had him spend the night. The weather tonight is going to be rough.”
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0004 }

“My belief is that he will arrive at Echo Cottage prior to the rain becoming particularly severe. In any case, returning this evening was his desire. Indeed, my stay was marvelous, though returning to you beloved people brings me joy. ‘East, west, hame’s best.’ Robin, is it the case that you have grown taller again recently?”
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0005 }

“Since you departed, I have grown an entire inch,” Robin said with pride. “Now I am just as tall as Milty Gammon. Am I not happy. Being bigger is something he will have to cease boasting about. Tell me, Nell, were you aware that Hugh Carrow is passing away?” Looking at Robin, Nell remained completely still and quiet. Thirza believed she would swoon because her face had turned so pale.
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0006 }

“Robin, keep quiet,” Mrs. Agatha uttered with anger. “Nell, stop making that face—stop making that face! Our intention was not to inform you with such suddenness.”
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0007 }

“Is—it—true?” Nell questioned using a voice that did not belong to her.
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0008 }

“Hugh is extremely sick,” Mrs. Sowerby stated solemnly. “Right after you departed for Echo Cottage, he came down with typhoid fever. Were you never told about it?”
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0009 }

“No,” replied the unidentified voice.
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0010 }

“From the beginning, it was an extremely severe situation. His health had been severely depleted, according to the physician. A professional nurse is present, and every possible measure has been taken. Do not wear that expression, Nell. As long as life remains, hope persists.”
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0011 }

“Mr. Pettifer was present tonight and he stated that they possessed no expectation for him,” Robin repeated.
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0012 }

Thirza, who appeared weary, aged, and exhausted, stood up and sternly escorted Robin out of the kitchen.
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0013 }

“Oh, do not have that expression, dear,” Mrs. Agatha said, placing her gentle, aged arms around the pale girl. “I really have not surrendered hope, I truly have not. He has the advantage of the Carrow constitution, that is the thing.”
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0014 }

Nell softly disengaged herself from Mrs. Sowerby’s embrace, navigated the kitchen without seeing, passed through the hall, and climbed the staircase to the bedroom that had been hers. Kneeling by its window, she gazed outside with eyes that saw nothing. Darkness hung heavily everywhere. Over the quivering fields, rain poured ceaselessly. The Haunted Woods echoed with the moaning of huge trees twisted by the storm, while the air vibrated with the deafening roar of waves breaking against the far-off coast. And Hugh was on the brink of death!
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0015 }

Just as the Bible contains a book of Revelation, so does the life of every individual. As Nell maintained her agonizing watch throughout the hours of darkness and storm on that bitter night, she read her own. She loved Hugh—she had loved him always! That was clear to her now. She recognized that casting him from her life without agony was no more possible than severing her right hand and throwing it away would be. Yet this realization had arrived too late—too late for even the bitter comfort of standing beside him in his final moments. Had she not been so blind—so foolish—she would now possess the right to join him. Instead, he would pass from this life believing she did not care, never knowing that she loved him. Oh, the dark, empty years unfolding ahead of her! Living through them was impossible—she simply could not! Cowering by her window, she wished that she could die as well, a desire she had never felt before in her gay young life. Should Hugh depart from her without a single word, sign, or message, her life could not continue. Without him, nothing held any value. She was his, and he was hers. During this moment of ultimate agony, she harbored no doubt regarding that truth. He did not love Rowena Calder—he had never loved Rowena Calder. Oh, what a fool she was for failing to see the nature of the bond tying her to Hugh—for mistaking the flattered fancy she harbored for Cyril Lisle for true love. And now, as if it were a crime, her folly demanded payment.
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0016 }

Prior to retiring for the night, Mrs. Sowerby and Thirza stole up to her doorway, silently exchanged uncertain nods at the quietness, and departed. Throughout the night the tempest continued furiously, yet it had exhausted itself by the time morning arrived. Nell observed a delicate, enchanted border of brightness along the edges of the night. Shortly thereafter, a glowing, ruby-like edge appeared upon the crests of the eastern hills. The clouds gathered into huge, gentle, pale heaps along the skyline as they moved off; the heavens shone with a silvery, azure light. A quietness descended upon the earth.
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0017 }

Rising from her knees, Nell crept downstairs. As she stepped into the yard, the cool, fresh rain-wind blew against her pale face, soothing her dry and burning eyes. Up the lane, a cheerful, buoyant whistle was echoing. Shortly after, Pacifique Buote appeared in view.
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0018 }

Without warning, Nell lost her bodily vigor. She had to grab a low willow branch to prevent herself from dropping down. Pacifique worked as a hired hand for Laurence Fletcher, whose residence was adjacent to the Carrows'. Mrs. Fletcher was the aunt of Hugh. Pacifique was sure to be aware if—if—Pacifique would be informed about whatever might be learned.
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0019 }

Pacifique was stepping along the red lane with a sturdy stride, whistling as he went. He failed to notice Nell. Three times she tried to call out to him in vain. He had nearly walked by when she finally managed to get her trembling lips to cry, “Pacifique!”
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0020 }

Pacifique offered a pleasant morning greeting as he swung around with a smile.
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0021 }

“Pacifique,” Nell asked weakly, “was it from Laurence Fletcher’s that you arrived earlier today?”
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0022 }

“Sure,” Pacifique said agreeably. “Las’ night I got de word dat my fader was seeck. Dat I couldn’t go den was because it was so stormy, so dis mornin’ I start vair early. For short cut, I’m goin’ troo de woods.”
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0023 }

“Was there any news about how Hugh Carrow was doing this morning?” Her overwhelming desperation forced the question from Nell. Bearing even the direst outcome would prove easier than continuing to suffer through this dreadful uncertainty.
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0024 }

“He is improving,” stated Pacifique. “He passed de turning point las’ night. De doctor claims he will recover fully in a short time now. It was a narrow escape, however! Dat boy, he almost killed himself at college. Well, I have to make haste. De old man, he will be eager to meet me.”
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0025 }

Pacifique restarted his strolling and his whistling. Nell watched him walk away with eyes in which the night's tense agony was being expelled by delight. He was an exceedingly tall and thin, exceedingly tattered, exceedingly plain young man. Yet to her eyes he possessed the beauty of those bearing glad tidings upon the mountains. For the rest of her life, Nell would never behold Pacifique’s dark-skinned, circular, dark-eyed countenance without a affectionate memory of the instance in which he had bestowed upon her the oil of gladness instead of grief.
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0026 }

It was long after Pacifique’s cheerful piping had dissolved into an echo of melody and subsequently into stillness far away beneath the maple trees of Linger Lane that Nell remained beneath the willows, savoring how intensely sweet life feels once a major terror has been lifted from it. The morning resembled a vessel brimming with fog and magic. In the nook close to her lay a lavish wonder of newly opened roses coated in crystal dew. The warbles and drips of music coming from the birds perched in the large tree over her appeared to be in complete harmony with how she felt. A phrase originating from a remarkably ancient, deeply accurate, incredibly marvelous Book rose to her lips,
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0027 }

“Sorrow might last through the night, yet happiness arrives with the dawn.”
{: #nw-v03-c40-p0028 }
